runs.v: According to the New Jersey Uniform Construction Code (N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7), a complete re-roof or tear-off on a detached one- or two-family home in Bloomfield is

That

exemption covers the roof covering only. On commercial buildings, condominiums, townhouses, and other attached or multi-family structures, the same code treats roofing as ordinary maintenance up to 25 percent of the roof area in a 12-month period; work beyond that threshold requires a permit. That threshold is what most people mean by the 25% rule for roofing. Roofers also use 25% as a rule of thumb: roof replacement may be necessary for older roofs with widespread damage, and once damage covers more than about a quarter of a roof, replacement usually makes more sense than another round of repairs. Structural work — cutting or replacing load-bearing framing or altering the roof structure — always requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7(b), regardless of building type. Bloomfield applies that state code, so roof replacements on commercial, attached, and larger multi-family buildings, and major structural repairs on any building, require specific permits.

When a permit applies, New Jersey's Rehabilitation Subcode (N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4) calls for full removal of the existing covering, with no recover-over, when the roof is water-soaked or deteriorated, when the covering is wood shake, slate, clay, cement, or asbestos-cement tile, or when two or more layers already exist, so a third layer of asphalt shingles is not allowed.

sections.heading: Roofing FAQs from Bloomfield, NJ Property Owners

faqs.q: Do you need a permit to replace a roof in Bloomfield, NJ?

runs.v: Not for a detached one- or two-family home: re-roofing it is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7. A commercial, multi-family, or attached building needs a permit from the Township of Bloomfield's construction office once work exceeds 25% of the roof area in 12 months, as does any structural change to rafters or trusses.

faqs.q: Does a historic district in Bloomfield restrict roofing work?

runs.v: It can. Properties in a historic district can need extra review of exterior materials before roofing work, so owners near Bloomfield Green and elsewhere confirm a parcel's status with the Bloomfield construction office before work starts. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private property owner.

faqs.q: What roofing material works best on a Bloomfield two-family or garden apartment?

faqs.q: Does homeowners insurance cover roof damage in Bloomfield?

runs.v: Usually, when a covered peril such as wind, hail, or a falling tree causes the damage; policies exclude normal wear, age, and deferred maintenance. Wind and hail rank as the largest homeowners-insurance claim type at 2.8% of insured homes per year, per the Insurance Information Institute, and Newark Quality Roofing documents storm damage with timestamped photographs for the adjuster.

runs.v: About 30 years for architectural shingles and about 20 years for 3-tab, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart. Clearing valleys and gutters and resealing flashing keeps a tree-shaded Bloomfield roof in that range.

sections.heading: How to Choose a Roofing Company in Bloomfield, NJ

runs.v: Bloomfield homeowners can check a roofing company in a few minutes. New Jersey home improvement contractors must register with the New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs, and the state has no separate roofing license, so verify a roofer by its New Jersey Home Improvement Contractor registration number. Registered contractors must also carry liability insurance, and those with employees must carry workers' compensation insurance, so ask for a certificate of insurance before you hire. Whether a roofer is a national franchise or locally owned, read its review history, check the Better Business Bureau's directory of roofing contractors serving Bloomfield, and ask neighbors whether their roofer completed the work on schedule.

Before signing, get a detailed, written estimate that specifies materials and project scope, and compare multiple estimates so each covers the same project details; many roofing companies also sell siding and windows for other home improvement needs, so make sure every bid prices the same roofing scope. A reputable contractor manages local permits and inspections for the project and never asks for full payment upfront or before work begins. Get the warranty in writing too: contractor workmanship warranties on installation quality typically run 5 to 10 years, separate from the manufacturer's material warranty.

c.v: How to tell if a roofer is lying?

runs.v: Watch for a price that changes without a written reason, pressure to sign on the spot, a large cash deposit before materials arrive, door-knockers after a nor'easter, and damage the roofer will not photograph. Some roofers advertise a 25-point roof inspection; whatever the checklist, a real inspection identifies the necessary repairs with a photograph of each. A trusted roofing contractor explains its findings clearly and puts the full scope in writing. GAF Master Elite is the highest level of GAF contractor certification, held by only about 2% of roofing contractors, per GAF, and GAF Master Elite contractors offer GAF's strongest lifetime limited warranties; Newark Quality Roofing is GAF-certified, so ask any roofer which GAF tier it holds.
